source.author: cic
source.text: appellant hoc Graeci, nos dicamus sane decorum; de quo praeclare et multa praecipiuntur et res est cognitione dignissima; huius ignoratione non modo in vita sed saepissime et in poematis et in oratione peccatur.
source.text_original: πρέπον appellant hoc Graeci, nos dicamus sane decorum; de quo praeclare et multa praecipiuntur et res est cognitione dignissima; huius ignoratione non modo in vita sed saepissime et in poematis et in oratione peccatur.
source.text_english: The Greeks call this prepon; let us, if you will, call it decorum. On this subject there are many excellent precepts, and it is a matter most worthy of knowledge; through ignorance of it, mistakes are made not only in life but very often in poems too and in oratory.

reuse.author: hier
reuse.text: et quia ualde prudens erat et nouerat illud, quod appellant philosophi , id est decere, quod facias, sic interrogata respondebat, ut etiam sua non sua diceret, sed uel mea uel cuiuslibet alterius, ut et in ipso, quod docebat, se discipulam fateretur sciebat enim dictum ab apostolo: docere autem mulieri non permitto , ne uirili sexui et interdum sacerdotibus de obscuris et ambiguis sciscitantibus facere uideretur iniuriam.
reuse.text_original: et quia ualde prudens erat et nouerat illud, quod appellant philosophi τὸ πρέπον, id est decere, quod facias, sic interrogata respondebat, ut etiam sua non sua diceret, sed uel mea uel cuiuslibet alterius, ut et in ipso, quod docebat, se discipulam fateretur — sciebat enim dictum ab apostolo: docere autem mulieri non permitto —, ne uirili sexui et interdum sacerdotibus de obscuris et ambiguis sciscitantibus facere uideretur iniuriam.
reuse.text_english: And because she was very prudent and knew what the philosophers call that is, what is becoming, namely to do what you do, when questioned she answered in such a way that she would call even her own things not her own, but either mine or someone else’s, so that in the very thing she was teaching she would confess herself to be a disciple; for she knew the saying of the apostle: But I do not permit a woman to teach, lest she seem to do wrong to the male sex and sometimes to priests who inquire about obscure and ambiguous matters.
